_help: Extra facts shown on ship cards. Key = ship name exactly as broadcast (capitals). Optional fields: cargo (what it usually carries), note (a fun fact), photo (link to a .jpg you have permission to use), photoCredit. Edit on GitHub and commit.

PAUL R. TREGURTHA.cargo: Usually coal, often from Superior's Midwest Energy terminal
PAUL R. TREGURTHA.note: The longest ship on the Great Lakes at 1,013.5 ft, nicknamed the "Queen of the Lakes".

EDWIN H. GOTT.note: A 1,004-ft laker in the Great Lakes Fleet.

STEWART J. CORT.note: The first 1,000-footer on the Great Lakes, launched in 1972.

ARTHUR M. ANDERSON.note: The last ship in radio contact with the Edmund Fitzgerald before it sank in November 1975.

PRESQUE ISLE.note: A 1,000-ft tug-barge: a tug locked into a notch at the back of the barge.

HON. JAMES L. OBERSTAR.note: Named for the Minnesota congressman who championed Great Lakes shipping.

ALDER.cargo: No cargo: U.S. Coast Guard buoy tender
ALDER.note: USCGC Alder is based in Duluth. It tends navigation buoys and breaks ice in winter.
